regret_risk: If a second tracker never arrives, the team keeps a port with one real adapter. The cost is a thin layer and a fake adapter, and the callers stay clean. If the port has the shape of beads, a Linear or Jira adapter forces a port change late. The regret also sits in the unverified claims. The cloud clone claim decides the shared backlog, and the Linear and Jira rows decide the later programs.
summary: The design puts a tracker port between CoBuilder and the task system. Beads is the first adapter and the master of programs, epics, slices, and pull requests. One projector keeps the index shape, and a fake adapter and one contract test prove the seam. Draft review round 1 found gaps, and the fixes landed. The cloud clone, bd claim, and the Linear and Jira rows have no test yet. The verdict stays concerns.
constraint_introduced: Readers and writers of workflow state call the tracker port, never a tracker CLI or API. Only an adapter knows a tracker. Every state write needs a configured adapter, and the tracker record wins over any file. Without an adapter, scripts read the file sources and refuse to write state.

findings.title: The mapping is total over the four stateful kinds
findings.detail: Programs, epics, slices, and pull requests each map to a record with a field-level home. Gates are program scalars. ADRs, designs, evidence, districts, and publications stay files with pointers. Nothing in the index loses its source.

findings.title: The viewer rule survives untouched
findings.detail: build_index.py keeps writing data/index.json, and the viewer keeps reading it static. The projector is one more source beside the file walkers, so ADR-0001 and ADR-0020 hold without amendment. A byte compare of the viewer file checks it.

findings.title: No test verifies the central store for cloud sessions
findings.detail: The success measure needs a fresh session to find a program with one list-programs call and the next slice with one next-ready call. A cloud session that holds only a git clone must run bd init and bd sync against refs/dolt/data. No test covers that case. If it fails, the shared backlog fails with it. The smoke check gates E2.

findings.title: The port may take the shape of beads
findings.detail: Beads is the only real adapter, so the port can leak beads words such as ready and claim. The port now has sync, claim_slice with an assignee, next_ready with a kind, and pull request operations. Capability flags, the fake adapter, and one contract test guard against the rest. The goal aborts if a method that only one tracker can implement cannot be a capability flag.
cites: shared boundary rule: no plugin import in shared

findings.title: The bd bridges cannot stand in for an adapter
findings.detail: No bridge pushes metadata.cb. A Jira pull that changes a mapped field replaces the metadata column. A Linear pull replaces it only for an issue with a project milestone. The state would stay in beads, so a Jira-only team would still need beads. The bridge is a mirror at best.

findings.title: A flat custom-data slot changes the envelope
findings.detail: Linear attachment metadata takes only a string or a number. The envelope rule allows a list of paths in cb.evidence. A Linear adapter must encode the list as a JSON string, and the value-level round trip test must pass it. The Jira slot takes any JSON, with a size limit.

findings.title: No tracker gives a verified atomic claim
findings.detail: Linear and Jira have no compare-and-set field, and bd claim has not run. The port reports atomic_claim as a capability. When it is false, claim_slice writes the claimant and reads the assignee back. Two sessions on one ladder can still race until that read lands. The claimant is a GitHub login, and how Linear and Jira resolve it to a user is not verified.

findings.title: The offline rule relaxes for later adapters
findings.detail: A Linear or Jira adapter needs the network, and Linear limits an API key to 2,500 requests an hour. The port has no snapshot. Such an adapter may cache inside itself, and the later programs decide. The offline_read flag tells a caller whether the rebuild can run with no network. The engineer accepted the relaxation on 2026-10-17.

findings.title: A configured adapter is a hard dependency of every state write
findings.detail: No script writes workflow state today. Agents edit the status files by hand, so the change adds the first scripted writers. After this design a missing adapter, and with beads a missing bd, blocks every state write. Scripts still read the file sources, so a degraded session can see state. The install command and implement:start must check for the adapter and say so.

findings.title: A pull request issue shows in bd ready until a human closes it
findings.detail: The pull request issue blocks its epics, so the epics stay out of bd ready until it closes. The issue itself appears as ready work, so next_ready and every consumer filter on metadata.cb.kind. A human closes the issue until gh:pr automation lands. The issue holds only the number and the merged bit, so GitHub stays the source of every other fact.

findings.title: The tracker wins, so a hand edit of a stateful line is overwritten
findings.detail: seed-from-files reads a file only to create a missing record. After that, the generator rewrites the stateful lines of each file from the tracker and reports a hand edit before it overwrites it. Until E3 and E4 land, the tables and the tracker can disagree. The cutover must flip authority in one commit.

findings.title: bd init must not install agent files or git hooks
findings.detail: By default, bd init installs an agent skill, Cursor rules, and git hooks. That would breach the install surface in the narrated repo. Both callers, implement:start at Gate 3 and the install command, run it with --skip-agents --skip-hooks, and the first asks for consent.

findings.title: The port keeps the base layer and the install surface intact
findings.detail: shared/tracker_port/ imports no plugin code, and an adapter calls a tool the way scripts call git and gh. No MCP server ships. verify_gate.py keeps importing only slice_table from shared and reaches the tracker through the port. A grep test checks that no script outside shared/tracker_port/ calls bd. One projector replaces the state parsing spread over twelve readers.
cites: shared boundary rule: no plugin import in shared
implement boundary rule: verify_gate.py imports only slice_table from shared

findings.title: Custom type budget is one
findings.detail: Only programs need a custom type, and only in the beads adapter. Epics, slices, and pull requests use built-in types. The gate approvals are scalar fields, and the ADR is a file. If a second custom type appears, the vocabulary was misread, and the mapping needs a new review.

findings.title: E1 ships alone only with a read-only files adapter
findings.detail: E1 holds the port, the projector, the fake adapter, the files adapter, and the contract test. The files adapter reuses slice_table, so the projector can match data/index.json offline before any bd call exists. Without it, E1 would have only a fake adapter and no parity check against the real corpus.

findings.title: Each done_when item needs an observable check
findings.detail: The goal now names six checks. They are a refused write, a grep check for the port rule, and a next_ready run with the file sources removed. They also include a byte compare of the viewer, a value-level round trip, and a check of the epics[] shape. The contract test has a case list in ADR-0040. Checked-in fixtures in tests/fixtures/tracker/ are the only test data. A check that stays unwritten is a step that gets skipped.

findings.title: The attempt stays a field and not a record
findings.detail: Each attempt could be a child record of the slice. No tracker has a natural child type for run history, and 96 slices would grow into several times as many issues. The slice keeps the latest score and the count. Evidence files and one dated comment keep each attempt. record_attempt is the single write, so a later child record needs no caller change.

findings.title: The reference and the skills can drift apart
findings.detail: Four skills link one shared reference, and many step procedures name its commands. A renamed command or a copied table leaves a stale instruction that agents follow. The guard is tests/test_tracker_docs.py. The reference must exist and each skill must link it, and each named command must be a listed subcommand. Only the beads notes may name bd. The pr and artifact skills are in scope, because they touch state at the same moments.
cites: pillar boundary test: a skill names no other skill's files, and the vendored shared/ is allowed

findings.title: An exported skill copy needs shared/ beside it
findings.detail: scripts/export-agent-skills.sh now copies shared/ and rewrites each plugin-root path to a relative path, so a harness other than Claude Code can reach the reference and the CLI. A temporary export left no plugin-root path and resolved all 40 relative paths. The copy still needs uv to run tracker.py, and no other harness has run it.
